brand_names: Certain Dri Clinical Strength Prescription Protection Roll-On
purpose: This product is used to treat excessive sweating, a condition called hyperhidrosis. It works by blocking your sweat glands to significantly reduce sweating, especially in the underarms. It is stronger than regular over-the-counter deodorants or antiperspirants.
how_it_works: The active ingredient, aluminum chloride, works by forming a plug inside your sweat gland ducts, which physically blocks sweat from reaching the surface of your skin. Think of it like a tiny cork stopping a bottle. Over time, with regular use, your sweating in the treated area will decrease noticeably.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are skin irritation, itching, burning, or tingling at the application site. Some people may notice temporary redness or a mild rash. These effects are usually mild and tend to improve as your skin gets used to the product.
warnings: Apply only to completely dry skin, ideally at bedtime, and wash it off in the morning — applying to wet skin greatly increases the chance of irritation. Do not use on broken, irritated, or recently shaved skin. Keep it away from your eyes, mouth, and clothing, as it can cause staining. If severe irritation, swelling, or rash develops, stop using it and contact your doctor or pharmacist.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer to clean, completely dry underarm skin at bedtime, usually 2 to 3 times per week to start. Once your sweating is under control, you may only need to use it once a week or as directed by your doctor. Always wash the area thoroughly in the morning before applying any other products.
